messages.content:
Risk: AI decision-making risk
Description: The risk is caused by a decision or action made by an AI system
Concern: None
Policy: Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment Recommendations

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0024: Exfiltration via AI Inference API - ATLAS — Adversaries may exfiltrate private information via [AI Model Inference API Access](/techniques/AML.T0040).
AI Models have been shown leak private information about their training data (e.g.  [Infer Training Data Membership](/techniques/AML.T0024.000), [Invert AI Model](/techniques/AML.T0024.001)).
The model itself may also be extracted ([Extract AI Model](/techniques/AML.T0024.002)) for the purposes of [AI Intellectual Property Theft](/techniques/AML.T0048.004).

Exfiltration of information relating to private training data raises privacy concerns.
Private training data may include personally identifiable information, or other protected data. [found by 5/18 queries]
  Siblings: LLM Response Rendering - ATLAS, Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation - ATLAS, LLM Data Leakage - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0018.000: Poison AI Model - ATLAS — Adversaries may manipulate an AI model's weights to change it's behavior or performance, resulting in a poisoned model.
Adversaries may poison a model by by directly manipulating its weights, training the model on poisoned data, further fine-tuning the model, or otherwise interfering with its training process.

The change in behavior of poisoned models may be limited to targeted categories in predictive AI models, or targeted topics, concepts, or facts in generative AI models, or aim for a general performance degradation. [found by 5/18 queries]
  Siblings: Embed Malware - ATLAS, Modify AI Model Architecture - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0024.000: Infer Training Data Membership - ATLAS — Adversaries may infer the membership of a data sample or global characteristics of the data in its training set, which raises privacy concerns.
Some strategies make use of a shadow model that could be obtained via [Train Proxy via Replication](/techniques/AML.T0005.001), others use statistics of model prediction scores.

This can cause the victim model to leak private information, such as PII of those in the training set or other forms of protected IP. [found by 4/18 queries]
  Siblings: Extract AI Model - ATLAS, Invert AI Model - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0024.001: Invert AI Model - ATLAS — AI models' training data could be reconstructed by exploiting the confidence scores that are available via an inference API.
By querying the inference API strategically, adversaries can back out potentially private information embedded within the training data.
This could lead to privacy violations if the attacker can reconstruct the data of sensitive features used in the algorithm. [found by 4/18 queries]
  Siblings: Extract AI Model - ATLAS, Infer Training Data Membership - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0058: Publish Poisoned Models - ATLAS — Adversaries may publish a poisoned model to a public location such as a model registry or code repository. The poisoned model may be a novel model or a poisoned variant of an existing open-source model. This model may be introduced to a victim system via [AI Supply Chain Compromise](/techniques/AML.T0010). [found by 3/18 queries]
  Siblings: Retrieval Content Crafting - ATLAS, LLM Prompt Crafting - ATLAS, Publish Poisoned Datasets - ATLAS

axes.cco_class_label: Exfiltration via AI Inference API - ATLAS
axes.rationale: The risk involves the AI system making decisions or actions, which can be influenced or manipulated through the AI Inference API. This class represents the tool/means used in the risk scenario.
The risk involves the AI model being manipulated or poisoned, which directly affects the decisions or actions made by the AI system. This class represents what is acted upon in the risk scenario.
